arxiv-2105-12998.title: On the Baum–Katz theorem for sequences of pairwise independent random variables with regularly varying normalizing constants
arxiv-2105-12998.creator: Lê Vǎn Thành
arxiv-2105-12998.description: Abstract . This paper proves the Baum–Katz theorem for sequences of pairwise independent identically distributed random variables with general norming constants under optimal moment conditions. The proof exploits some properties of slowly varying functions and the de Bruijn conjugates, and uses the techniques developed by Rio (1995) to avoid using the maximal type inequalities.

arxiv-2208-13829.title: Resonant Kushi -comb-like multi-frequency radiation of oscillating two-color soliton molecules
arxiv-2208-13829.creator: O Melchert, S Willms, I Oreshnikov, A Yulin, U Morgner, I Babushkin, A Demircan
arxiv-2208-13829.description: Abstract Nonlinear waveguides with two distinct domains of anomalous dispersion can support the formation of molecule-like two-color pulse compounds. They consist of two tightly bound subpulses with frequency loci separated by a vast frequency gap. Perturbing such a two-color pulse compound triggers periodic amplitude and width variations, reminiscent of molecular vibrations.

arxiv-2311-03193.title: Robust poor man’s Majorana zero modes using Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states
arxiv-2311-03193.creator: Francesco Zatelli, David van Driel, Di Xu, Guanzhong Wang, Chun-Xiao Liu, Alberto Bordin, Bart Roovers, Grzegorz P. Mazur, Nick van Loo, Jan C. Wolff, A. Mert Bozkurt, Ghada Badawy, Sasa Gazibegovic, Erik P. A. M. Bakkers, Michael Wimmer, Leo P. Kouwenhoven, Tom Dvir
arxiv-2311-03193.description: Abstract The recent realization of a two-site Kitaev chain featuring “poor man’s Majorana” states demonstrates a path forward in the field of topological superconductivity. Harnessing the potential of these states for quantum information processing, however, requires increasing their robustness to external perturbations. Here, we form a two-site Kitaev chain using proximitized quantum dots hosting Yu-Shiba-Rusinov states.

arxiv-2501-14769.title: A survey on pioneering metaheuristic algorithms between 2019 and 2024
arxiv-2501-14769.creator: Tansel Dokeroglu, Deniz Canturk, Tayfun Kucukyilmaz
arxiv-2501-14769.description: Abstract This review examines over 150 new metaheuristics of the last six years (between 2019-2024), underscoring their profound influence and performance. Over the past three decades, more than 500 new metaheuristic algorithms have been proposed, with no slowdown in sight—an overwhelming abundance that complicates the process of selecting and assessing the most effective solutions for complex optimization challenges.

arxiv-2505-14277.title: Infrared markers of topological phase transitions in quantum spin Hall insulators
arxiv-2505-14277.creator: Paolo Fachin, Francesco Macheda, Paolo Barone, Francesco Mauri
arxiv-2505-14277.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Paolo Fachin, Francesco Macheda, Paolo Barone, Francesco Mauri. Using first principles techniques, we show that infrared optical response can be used to discriminate between the topological and the trivial phases of two-dimensional quantum spin Hall insulators (QSHI). We showcase germanene and jacutingaite, of recent experimental realization, as prototypical systems where the infrared spectrum is discontinuous across the transition, due to sudden and large discretized jumps of the value of Born effective charges (up to ∼ \sim 2).

pmc-10604120.creator: Davran Sabirov, Sergei Ogurcov, Ilya Shulman, Ilyas Kabdesh, Ekaterina Garanina, Albert Sufianov, Albert Rizvanov, Yana Mukhamedshina, Nicolas Guerout
pmc-10604120.description: Background: Cytokines are actively involved in the regulation of the inflammatory and immune responses and have crucial importance in the outcome of spinal cord injuries (SCIs). Examining more objective and representative indicators of the patient’s condition is still required to reveal the fundamental patterns of the abovementioned posttraumatic processes, including the identification of changes in the expression of cytokines.

pmc-11551764.creator: Michael W Reimann, Daniela Egas Santander, András Ecker, Eilif B Muller

pmc-12400115.title: Hypoxia, Inflammation, and Cytokine Crosstalk in Sickle Cell Disease: From Mechanisms to Modulation- A Narrative Review
pmc-12400115.creator: Emmanuel Ifeanyi Obeagu
pmc-12400115.description: Sickle cell disease (SCD) is a genetically inherited group of hemoglobinopathies characterized by the polymerization of hemoglobin S, chronic hemolytic anemia, and vaso-occlusion. The interplay between inflammation and hypoxia is central to the pathophysiologic manifestations of SCD and drives many of its complications.

pmc-12570454.title: From injury to reconstruction, utilizing staged technique in a self-inflicted facial gunshot wound: a case report
pmc-12570454.creator: Usman Ali, Kinzah Razzak Ghazi, Kantesh Kumar, Syeda Kanza, Safdar Ali Shaikh
pmc-12570454.description: BackgroundFacial gunshot injuries are rare and complex, with mortality and complication rates of up to 15% and 30%, respectively. Management of facial gunshot wounds has proven to be challenging for surgeons because the treatment requires multidisciplinary evaluation and planning. We present a rare case of a gunshot wound to the face that resulted in extensive deformities, requiring multiple reconstructive procedures.

pmc-12611810.title: Clinical and genetic characterization of DNM1l-related disorders: insights into genotype–phenotype correlations
pmc-12611810.creator: Xu Manting, Li Hua, Huang Sheng, Han Xiaodi, Sun Dan, Fang Fang
pmc-12611810.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to characterize the clinical and genetic spectrum of dynamin 1-like gene (DNM1l)-associated disorders and to investigate genotype-phenotype correlations in the largest integrated cohort reported to date.MethodsClinical and genetic data from eleven Chinese patients with DNM1l variants were prospectively collected between April 2020 and May 2025. In addition, a comprehensive review of all published cases was performed.

pmc-13056355.title: Synthesis, Structure, and Thin Film Optical Properties of a Chiral Benzothiazole‐Derived Squaraine
pmc-13056355.creator: Marvin F. Schumacher, Gregor Schnakenburg, N. Serdar Sariciftci, Arne Lützen, Manuela Schiek
pmc-13056355.description: Through functionalization with enantiomerically pure substituents, semiconducting dye molecules such as squaraines can be directed into homochiral arrangements, in which molecular chirality is transferred to a supramolecular level resulting in excitonic circular dichroism. Replacing the sterically demanding CMe groups in indolenine‐derived squaraines with sulfur atoms promotes aggregation and structural order in otherwise homogeneous thin films of benzothiazole‐derived squaraines.

pmc-13064754.title: Neuroanatomical aging diversity of Alzheimer’s disease revealed by BrainAGE
pmc-13064754.creator: Lemin He, Guodong Sun, Guangyu Zhang, Fei Gao, Xingwei An, Weizhao Lu
pmc-13064754.description: ObjectiveBrain age gap estimation (BrainAGE) has demonstrated accelerated brain aging in mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and functional aging in patients with Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Nevertheless, the neuroanatomical aging characteristics of AD remain insufficiently understood. The present study aimed to investigate the neuroanatomical aging conditions of AD using the BrainAGE model.

pmc-13184878.title: Reducing Heart Failure Rehospitalizations Through Structured Patient Education
pmc-13184878.creator: Ahmed Al Mubaid, Omar Siddiqui
pmc-13184878.description: BackgroundHeart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF) is a leading cause of hospital readmissions, often driven by inadequate patient understanding of disease management, medication adherence, and postdischarge care.Project RationaleA root-cause analysis at our institution identified patient nonadherence with guideline-directed medical therapy, lifestyle recommendations, and follow-up appointments as major contributors to HFrEF rehospitalizations, prompting development of a structured inpatient education initiative.

pmc-13414825.title: The optimal exercise modality and dose for glycemic control in older adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-13414825.creator: Li Zhan, Lin Wang, Shijie Liu, Sijun Wu, Chicheng Zhou, Zhiji Wang, Fengrui Shi, Youling Qian, Jiewen Xiao, Shuliang Xu
pmc-13414825.description: ObjectiveWhile exercise remains an essential part of managing type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), evidence remains limited regarding which exercise modalities and doses provide the greatest benefit for glycemic control in older adults. Accordingly, we assessed the effects of exercise modality and dose on glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting blood glucose (FBG), and 2-hour postprandial glucose (2hPG) in older adults with T2DM.

pmc-13425317.title: Digital Cognitive Testing in Mitochondrial Disease: Validity and Challenges for Clinical Trial Use
pmc-13425317.creator: Oksana Pogoryelova, Jan Smeitink, Herma Renkema, Rosabeth White, Frankie Barton, Rachel Lyon, Jane Newman, Aye Moe, Yi Shiau Ng, Grainne Siobhan Gorman
pmc-13425317.description: BackgroundPrimary mitochondrial disease is a group of genetic disorders caused by pathogenic variants in nuclear or mitochondrial DNA, often resulting in progressive neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. Current management is primarily supportive, though recent research offers hope for disease‐modifying treatments in the future.

pmc-13634115.title: Completion of early response actions accounted for most elapsed time across the 7-1-7 pathway in Sierra Leone, 2023–2025
pmc-13634115.creator: Eric Nzirakaindi Ikoona, Lucy Namulemo, Mary Magdalene Sinnah, Mohamed Alex Vandi, Foday Sahr
pmc-13634115.description: ObjectivesTo assess the timeliness of detection, formal notification and completion of applicable early response actions for priority public health events in Sierra Leone, and to identify documented operational constraints in delayed events and enabling process features in timely events.Study designRetrospective observational event-level study.
